proposals.title: When Museums Started Explaining Repair
proposals.researchQuestion: How did museum annual reports and public accountability documents change their language around provenance, restitution, repatriation, access, and community between 2000 and 2026?
proposals.whyItMatters: The existing museum-language artifact is ready as a source-caveated page study; annual reports would test whether public-facing web copy matches institutional self-reporting over time.
proposals.unitOfAnalysis: museum annual report section or paragraph snapshot
likelySources: Internet Archive snapshots for report indexes
requiredTransformations: PDF text extraction with page anchors
expectedChartsOrTables: source coverage table by museum and year
representativeRecordsNeeded: one pre-2010 annual report page per source where available
one no-signal control paragraph per museum
reasonsTheIdeaMightBeWrong: annual reports may be written for donors rather than public interpretation
PDF availability may be uneven by museum and year
report design and OCR quality may create artificial language shifts
proposals.firstRunnableCorpusBuild: Select 12 museums already present in museum-language-drift, fetch all public annual reports available for 2000-2026, extract text into paragraph records, and reuse the existing museum term taxonomy with a document-genre label.
proposals.publicEssayAngle: A follow-up to the museum language post: not just what museums say on web pages, but when repair and accountability entered their institutional record.

proposals.title: The Strategic Plan University
proposals.researchQuestion: Do university strategic plans show a stronger shift toward innovation, impact, global leadership, belonging, and workforce language than mission/about pages?
proposals.whyItMatters: Mission pages are stable public signals, but strategic plans are where universities describe intended change. Comparing the two source genres can separate institutional identity from managerial priorities.
likelySources: Internet Archive snapshots of plan pages
representativeRecordsNeeded: mission page and strategic plan from the same institution-year where possible
post-2020 plans with inclusion and workforce language
reasonsTheIdeaMightBeWrong: strategic plans may be episodic and not comparable year by year
universities may remove old plans from public sites
consultant-written plans can converge stylistically without reflecting institutional purpose
proposals.firstRunnableCorpusBuild: Use the 10 universities in university-mission-statement-drift, collect public strategic plans and president messages for 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2026 anchors, then compare against existing mission-page term families.
proposals.publicEssayAngle: Universities may not have changed what they say they are for as much as how they plan, manage, and justify themselves.

proposals.title: What Humanities AI Actually Studies
proposals.researchQuestion: Which corpora, archives, languages, periods, and media types appear most often in AI-for-humanities work from 2020 onward?
proposals.whyItMatters: The literature radar maps AI and quantitative humanities works, but the next public question is what cultural material those methods actually touch.
proposals.unitOfAnalysis: scholarly work to named corpus/archive/dataset mention
likelySources: paper full text where open and permitted
requiredTransformations: manual audit of high-frequency extracted entities
representativeRecordsNeeded: works using newspapers or social media
reasonsTheIdeaMightBeWrong: metadata abstracts may omit corpus names
full-text access may bias toward open preprints
named entity extraction can merge projects, datasets, and institutions incorrectly
proposals.firstRunnableCorpusBuild: Start from the 593 quantitative/computational candidates in humanities-literature-radar, extract corpus/entity mentions from titles and abstracts, then audit the top 100 mentions before scaling to open full text.
proposals.publicEssayAngle: AI in the humanities is not only a method trend; it is a map of which parts of culture are becoming computationally visible.

proposals.title: The Anthology Table Of Contents As Canon Sensor
proposals.researchQuestion: Can public anthology tables of contents and publisher previews measure author and work turnover across editions in a narrow literary field?
proposals.whyItMatters: The canon drift feasibility artifact says canon drift is multi-source. A bounded anthology pilot can test one signal deeply before making wider claims.
proposals.unitOfAnalysis: author-work appearance in an anthology edition table of contents
likelySources: Google Books snippets where permitted for bibliographic metadata
representativeRecordsNeeded: two or more editions of the same anthology
author-work rows with page or section evidence
reasonsTheIdeaMightBeWrong: tables of contents may be copyrighted or not publicly extractable at scale
anthologies differ in market and course level
edition changes can reflect permissions and price rather than canon judgment
proposals.firstRunnableCorpusBuild: Pick one anthology family with public TOC evidence across at least three editions, build an edition-level table, and compare against a small public syllabus control set without treating syllabi as representative.
proposals.publicEssayAngle: Canon drift becomes measurable only when the source is narrow enough to audit edition by edition.

proposals.title: The Afterlife Of Humanities Datasets
proposals.researchQuestion: What happens to public humanities datasets after release: do they get cited, forked, reused in papers, linked from projects, or quietly disappear?
proposals.whyItMatters: The dataset registry identifies ready-now corpora. A follow-up can test whether dataset quality predicts actual scholarly and public reuse.
representativeRecordsNeeded: datasets with broken links or access changes
ready-now datasets with no visible reuse
reasonsTheIdeaMightBeWrong: reuse is often informal and hard to observe
citations may attach to papers rather than datasets
older datasets may predate modern DOI and repository practices
proposals.firstRunnableCorpusBuild: Take the 15 dataset-registry candidates, collect DOI/URL/repository identifiers, query OpenAlex and repository metadata for reuse signals, and hand-audit the top and bottom cases.
proposals.publicEssayAngle: Humanities datasets are infrastructure, but their public afterlife is uneven and measurable.
